messages:
leah: quick proposal: instead of heavy manifest expansion, let the router do a cheap capability probe to the runtime to decide routing/fallbacks. goal = minimal manifest, late-binding of compatible variants.

omar: curious how this differs from the probe ideas we've seen? be explicit about cache keys + seq_len handling.

leah: two major pieces: (1) tiny /v1/capability-probe that takes model_id + seq_len_bucket + requested_features, returns supports[], compatible_variants[], cap_hash, and an advisory tier label (e.g. low/high cost). (2) router caching rules: cache by model_id+features_set+cap_hash+seq_bucket with small TTL.

sasha: seq_len_bucket? define buckets pls. probes at full seq_len risk cache explosion.

leah: proposed buckets: short (<=64), mid (65-512), long (>512). router can quantize incoming requests to these buckets. bucket membership included in probe request so runtime can respond with optimizations per latency class.

devon: agree on bucketization. operational note: router should not probe on every request. initial flow: try local cache -> if miss, async probe + optimistic routing to default variant -> once probe returns, reconcile. avoid holding the request for probe latency.

omar: that optimistic routing worries me for correctness (e.g., variant lacks kv_cache and responses change). fallback semantics?

leah: fallback tiers: immediate-compatible (runtime says this exact variant supports features), graceful-degrade (runtime lacks kv_cache but supports streaming; router can switch to degrade mode), and hard-fail (no compatible variant). Default policy: prefer immediate-compatible, if none, consult policy for graceful-degrade vs hard-fail. Router may consult a customer policy flag.

sasha: security: for Private/VPC runtime calls must be local only. For Hosted, probes originate from control-plane with attestation. no cross-tenant probing.

leah: yep. attestation model: control-plane signs a short-lived token containing client_id+cap_hash request. runtime validates signature and returns signed_cap_hash in response. runtime never returns raw kernel flags or perf counters, only boolean supports and stable identifiers.

billing-team: cost visibility ask: can we avoid exposing cost deltas that would confuse customers? Ops needs to surface explain-mode only.

leah: plan: include a non-default explain=true query param that returns cost_hint. By default probe responses omit cost info; routers only get cost hints if they run with explain mode (used in debug or rollout). billing-team: confirm that's ok.

ops-bot: note: loadtest can produce probe storms. recommend leaky-bucket rate limit per router instance + jittered backoff + shared cache layer in CP.

devon: implementation detail: cache key should include cap_hash to allow runtime to invalidate variants without TTL churn. cap_hash computed by runtime over capability set + model version. runtime increments hash on changes. cache eviction TTL small (30-120s) and we also honor runtime-provided ttl_seconds.

omar: what about probe storms during model rollout? e.g., new variant deployed to subset of nodes, cache miss everywhere. routers might flood runtime.

leah: mitigation: (1) router-local randomized jitter before first probe, (2) exponential backoff with capped attempts per model per minute, (3) allow CP shared cache or feature-store to serve probes for hosted mode. also add a probe-throttling header runtime can return when overwhelmed (Retry-After semantics).

sasha: test matrix: functional correctness (feature-negotiation), security (attestation + RBAC), load (probe storms), and billing (explain mode gating). I'm going to add a checklist.

billing-team: we'll need console flags to opt-in to using cost hints for routing and a way to audit fallback choices for invoices.

devon: telemetry: we need sample traces that link request -> probe_cap_hash -> chosen_variant so we can debug quality regressions. also expose counts of graceful-degrades.

leah: agreed. telemetry payload minimal: cap_hash, seq_bucket, features_requested, chosen_variant_id. no perf internals.

omar: rollout plan suggestion: start with internal tenants only, enable explain-mode, validate behavior under load, then stitch to billing for policy gating, then beta to customers.

sasha: ops readiness: add a CP shared-probe cache component that can short-circuit probes for hosted; include circuit-breaker on runtime if probe error rate > threshold.

leah: next steps: I'll write an RFC with schema example, TTL rules, seq_len buckets, caching algorithm, and attestation flow. I'll include failing-safe defaults and per-tenant policy knobs. target: prototype in staging next sprint.

devon: timeline ok. can we include a minimal runtime stub + router change that avoids request blocking? put that in the RFC too.

leah: yes will include non-blocking flow: return best-effort default immediately and reconcile post-probe for subsequent requests.

ops-bot: reminder: open incident channel if probe errors spike during canary.

leah: thanks all, will post RFC link here once done and tag reviewers. closing thread for now.
